title: Noor and the Asset
premise: Hazel Montrose, a sleep-ruined interpreter for a faltering peace delegation, is the only person who notices that Flight 447's records vanish mid-flight—and the only one who heard, through his headset, a phrase in an unlisted dialect that shouldn't exist. Pulled into the orbit of 'the Asset,' a defector who knows who erased the plane and why, Hazel uncovers a plot to stage a catastrophic 'accident' that will bury the peace process and consolidate power among those who inherited it. As the delegation collapses around him, Hazel must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the found family of colleagues who've become his only anchor. In the end he stops the attack at terrible cost—the Asset dies buying him time—but testifies before an inquiry, finally sleeping through the night.
about_author: Sebastian Sandoval is a former conference interpreter turned novelist who spent a decade working behind glass booths in Geneva and Vienna. He writes thrillers about the people history forgets: the translators, fixers, and witnesses standing just off-mic.

chapters.title: The Booth
chapters.summary: Hazel Montrose interprets a doomed negotiation session, exhausted and invisible, while delegates trade insults in three languages. POV: Hazel. Beat: establishes his insomnia, his precision, and his longing to stay unnoticed.

chapters.title: Static on Channel Two
chapters.summary: During a routine relay, Hazel hears a fragment in an unregistered dialect—'the ledger closes at dawn.' No one else logged it. POV: Hazel. Beat: unease; the first crack in his invisibility.

chapters.title: Flight 447
chapters.summary: The delegation's key witness boards a short flight home. Hazel watches the tracking feed out of habit. POV: Hazel. Beat: dread without evidence.

chapters.title: Vanishing Point
chapters.summary: Mid-air, every record of the flight evaporates: manifests, radar archives, even Hazel's own email confirming the booking. POV: Hazel. Beat: vertigo; reality itself feels edited.

chapters.title: Nobody Was on That Plane
chapters.summary: Officials deny the flight existed. Hazel's supervisor warns him to drop it—or be declared unstable. POV: Hazel. Beat: gaslighting; isolation begins.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Shouldn't Answer
chapters.summary: Hazel traces the dialect phrase to a retired linguist, Dr. Ilsa Rehn, who goes silent when he names it. POV: Hazel. Beat: hope curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: A note appears in Hazel's coat: a time, a tram stop, no signature. He goes anyway. POV: Hazel. Beat: fatalism; he's already committed.

chapters.title: The Asset
chapters.summary: He meets Marek Voss—a defected analyst who helped build the erasure system and now wants out. He calls himself 'the Asset.' POV: Hazel (with Marek's controlled reveal). Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Buys
chapters.summary: Marek explains: a cabal of inheritors—families and institutions profiting from perpetual conflict—plans a staged disaster to kill the peace deal. POV: alternating. Beat: scale revealed; stakes made personal.

chapters.title: Dawn, and a Harbor
chapters.summary: Marek identifies the target: a ferry carrying delegation families during the closing ceremony. Timeline: nine days. POV: Hazel. Beat: cold horror; the clock starts.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Hazel tries reporting through channels; his memo is intercepted within hours. Someone inside is watching. POV: Hazel. Beat: paranoia tightens.

chapters.title: Colonel Ash
chapters.summary: Security chief Colonel Ash takes Hazel under her wing—or seems to. She asks precise questions about 'his sources.' POV: Hazel. Beat: ambiguous protection.

chapters.title: The Found Family
chapters.summary: Interpreters' dinner: June the stenographer, old Tomas, young Priya. For one evening Hazel sleeps two hours without dreaming. POV: Hazel. Beat: warmth; what he stands to lose.

chapters.title: Tail
chapters.summary: Hazel spots surveillance on Priya. He leads the watchers away through the old quarter, nearly caught. POV: Hazel. Beat: fear sharpening into responsibility.

chapters.title: Rehn's Archive
chapters.summary: Dr. Rehn agrees to authenticate the dialect—for a price: Hazel smuggles her research out of a locked annex. POV: Hazel. Beat: complicity deepens.

chapters.title: The Dialect That Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: Rehn confirms the phrase belongs to a constructed language used only by the cabal's inner circle. The Asset was trained in it. POV: Hazel/Rehn. Beat: revelation; the enemy has a grammar.

chapters.title: Ash's Offer
chapters.summary: Colonel Ash reveals she knows about Marek—and offers Hazel immunity if he delivers him. POV: Hazel. Beat: betrayal looming; loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Safehouse
chapters.summary: Hazel warns Marek; they argue about trust. Marek admits he designed the erasure protocol himself. POV: both. Beat: fracture and repair; found family forged in guilt.

chapters.title: Eight Days
chapters.summary: They decode a partial manifest: the ferry attack requires a customs override signed inside the delegation. A traitor with access. POV: Hazel. Beat: narrowing circle.

chapters.title: June's Fingers
chapters.summary: Stenographer June quietly shows Hazel transcripts she was ordered to purge—including Flight 447's last transmission. POV: June/Hazel. Beat: courage of the overlooked.

chapters.title: The Last Transmission
chapters.summary: The recording proves the flight was diverted deliberately. Hazel now holds proof—but playing it exposes June. POV: Hazel. Beat: moral weight of evidence.

chapters.title: Seven Days
chapters.summary: Ash assigns Hazel a minder. He plays the obedient witness while passing data to Marek through interpreted 'errors.' POV: Hazel. Beat: double life; craft as resistance.

chapters.title: Tomas Falls
chapters.summary: Old Tomas is hospitalized after a 'mugging' that took only his notes. Hazel recognizes the warning for what it is. POV: Hazel. Beat: grief; the cost becomes flesh.

chapters.title: The Inheritors
chapters.summary: Marek names three heirs of the cabal, including a beloved elder statesman chairing the ceremony. POV: Marek/Hazel. Beat: disillusionment; power wears a kindly face.

chapters.title: Priya Asks Questions
chapters.summary: Priya, too curious, reconstructs the flight timeline on her own—and emails a colleague. Hazel must silence her before the watchers do. POV: Priya/Hazel. Beat: terror of innocence endangered.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Marek's safehouse is hit; they escape with minutes to spare but lose the archive copies. POV: both. Beat: desperation; everything now lives in their heads.

chapters.title: Five Days
chapters.summary: With no hard evidence left, Hazel proposes the unthinkable: let him be recruited by Ash fully, then turn her. POV: Hazel. Beat: gambler's resolve.

chapters.title: Double Agent
chapters.summary: Hazel feeds Ash curated truths, earning access to the security grid for the ceremony. POV: Hazel. Beat: tension of performance; every word weighted.

chapters.title: Ash Unmasked
chapters.summary: Marek decrypts Ash's traffic: she isn't cabal—she's hunting them from inside, alone, and has been since Flight 447 killed her brother. POV: Ash/Hazel. Beat: reversal; enemy becomes ally.

chapters.title: Four Hands, Four Days
chapters.summary: Ash, Hazel, Marek, and June form an improvised cell with no authority and four days. POV: rotating. Beat: found family weaponized.

chapters.title: The Override
chapters.summary: They trace the customs signature to the statesman's aide—who is found dead before they can move, silenced by his own side. POV: Hazel. Beat: futility; the machine eats its own.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Plan B: Marek can trigger a failsafe in the erasure system itself, forcing the cabal to abort rather than leave records. It requires physical access to the harbor control room. POV: Marek. Beat: sacrifice foreshadowed.

chapters.title: What Marek Owes
chapters.summary: Marek confesses he erased Flight 447 under orders before defecting; the failsafe is his penance. Hazel refuses to accept the plan's arithmetic. POV: both. Beat: guilt, forgiveness, argument.

chapters.title: Two Days
chapters.summary: Rehearsal day at the harbor. Hazel interprets for the statesman himself, close enough to touch the conspiracy's face. POV: Hazel. Beat: icy composure over panic.

chapters.title: One Day
chapters.summary: Final preparations. June will pull the fire alarm fallback; Ash locks down the pier; Hazel carries Marek's access chip in his shoe. POV: rotating. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Ceremony
chapters.summary: The closing ceremony begins. Hazel interprets peace speeches while watching the water, the clocks, the exits. POV: Hazel. Beat: unbearable normalcy.

chapters.title: The Ledger Closes
chapters.summary: The attack launches early. Marek reaches the control room and triggers the failsafe, exposing the operation's own records live; the strike team stands down as their orders become evidence. Marek doesn't make it out. POV: alternating. Beat: climax; victory purchased with blood.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Arrests ripple upward. The statesman falls. Hazel testifies, translating his own grief into the record. Ash and June stand witness beside him. POV: Hazel. Beat: catharsis; truth spoken aloud.

chapters.title: Sleep
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Hazel visits Marek's grave, teaches Priya relay technique, and—finally—sleeps through the night. Some inheritance you refuse. POV: Hazel. Beat: quiet resolution; dawn without dread.
